newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on hopes of improved economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on hopes of improved economy.

text.p: Thai stocks ended higher on Wednesday after buyers bought blue-chip stocks on expectations of signs of an improved economy, brokers said.
The SET index ended 11.25 points higher at 1,105.84 on 3.2 billion baht trade. Gainers led decliners 203 to 92 while 114 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index was 1.07 points higher to 84.63.

"The index rose after investors bought stocks on hopes that some of the key economic indicators to be released on Thursday would show the economy is improving," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.
Brokers said economic problems like a widening current account deficit and slowing economy were among the major reasons investors had stayed away from the market over the past two months.
"It's expected that today's buying of blue-chip stocks was for speculative reasons ahead of the release of key economic data," Somchai said.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising four baht to 218. Krung Thai Thanakit rose two to 110 and Siam Cement advanced 16 to 944.
